Class Focus

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.Focus
public final class Focus extends Object
Focus for widgets MenuKit places on a screen, and the "is this point covered by MenuKit" checks.

Panels eat clicks inside their bounds, and vanilla only moves focus when a widget in Screen.children() claims a click. So on a click in empty space, inside a panel or outside, nothing claims it, vanilla never calls Screen.setFocused(...), and a focused widget stays focused and keeps swallowing keystrokes. Two paths fix that:

  1. Clicks MenuKit takes: ScreenPanelRegistry calls blurOnOutsideBounds(Screen, double, double) after routing a click to a panel.
  2. Clicks vanilla handles: a Fabric ScreenMouseEvents.afterMouseClick listener, installed by init(), does the same after vanilla's dispatch.
Both only touch widgets registered through addWidget(Screen, T); other widgets on the screen keep vanilla's focus behavior.

The second path is a Fabric event rather than a mixin because in 26.2 Screen doesn't override mouseClicked; it inherits the default method from ContainerEventHandler, so there is no code in Screen.class to inject into.

For mods

To put a vanilla widget in a panel, use WidgetHost (7.2.0). It registers the widget here, routes its mouse input, and gives up focus when the widget is not shown. A widget a mod places itself goes through addWidget(Screen, T) rather than ScreenAccessor.mk$addWidget, since it adds the widget to the screen and opts it into this focus handling. Pair it with removeWidget(Screen, GuiEventListener).

clear(Screen) blurs whatever is focused, for starting an input mode from a clean state (chord capture, a modal confirm, handing navigation over).

Tracking is keyed weakly by Screen, so a collected screen drops out. The widgets in each set are held strongly, but the screen's own children list already keeps them alive as long.

  • Method Details

    • init

      public static void init()
      Registers the ScreenEvents.AFTER_INIT listener that adds the afterMouseClick focus check to every screen. Called once from MenuKitClient.onInitializeClient. The per-screen listeners go with their screen.

    • blurOnOutsideBounds

      public static void blurOnOutsideBounds(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Clears the screen's focus when the focused widget was registered through addWidget(Screen, T) and the click landed outside it. A click inside leaves focus alone: either vanilla moves focus to whatever claimed the click, or the widget keeps it (clicking a focused TextField again, say). Widgets not registered here keep vanilla's behavior.

      Called after vanilla's click dispatch (through the afterMouseClick listener) and after MenuKit routes a click to a panel. So clicking any MenuKit button or dropdown that doesn't take focus itself blurs a focused MenuKit text field, as vanilla does when another widget claims a click.

    • addWidget

      public static <T extends net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.GuiEventListener & net.minecraft.client.gui.narration.NarratableEntry> T addWidget(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, T widget)
      Adds a widget to the screen for input and opts it into MenuKit's focus handling. Through ScreenAccessor.mk$addWidget(T) the widget joins the screen's children and narratables lists, so vanilla sends it input, and it is recorded here, so a click outside it clears its focus.

      Returns the widget, as vanilla's addWidget does.

    • removeWidget

      public static void removeWidget(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.GuiEventListener widget)
      Undoes addWidget(Screen, T): removes the widget from the screen's input and from focus tracking. Does nothing for a widget that was never registered.

    • clear

      public static void clear(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen)
      Clears focus on the screen, the same as screen.setFocused(null). For a mod that wants a clean focus state, say before starting chord capture. MenuKit's click handling already clears focus in the cases above.

    • isManaged

      public static boolean isManaged(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.GuiEventListener widget)
      Whether the widget was registered on the screen through addWidget(Screen, T). The focus check and the widget hover suppressor use it; the suppressor skips registered widgets, so a TextField's wrapped EditBox keeps its hover and cursor feedback inside the panel it belongs to.

    • isCursorCovered

      public static boolean isCursorCovered(double mouseX, double mouseY)
      Whether vanilla content at the point is covered by MenuKit, by ScreenPanelRegistry.claimAt(Screen, double, double): a shown modal claims everything; an opaque panel claims its whole rectangle; a transparent panel its solid elements; an open popover its area. Across every host on the screen (container and vanilla-screen adapters, anchors, a standalone screen's own panels).

      One exception, for content that belongs to the screen itself (its widgets, list rows, tabs, tooltips): a standalone screen's own panels do not make that screen's own widgets inert (see ScreenPanelRegistry.screenContentInertAt(Screen, double, double)).

    • isCursorCoveredAtCursor

      public static boolean isCursorCoveredAtCursor()
      isCursorCovered(double, double) at the live cursor (GUI-scaled from MouseHandler).

    • isInertUnderPanel

      public static boolean isInertUnderPanel(double mouseX, double mouseY)
      The inertness check every suppressor of screen content uses (widget hover, list hover, creative tabs, tooltips), so they all agree on whether a point is covered. Slot hover asks the slot form, ScreenPanelRegistry.slotInertAt(Screen, double, double), which differs only in that a panel's own slot stays live under its own claim. The modal case is part of the claim.
